articleTitle: Design of robust H-infinity speed controller for high performance BLDC servo drive
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: In Brushless DC (BLDC) motors, commutation is done externally by using a three phase inverter and therefore need more complex control algorithm as compared to brushed DC motors. BLDC motors are found to be the most suitable actuator for high performance servo drive used in robotics, industrial automation, automobiles, aerospace etc. The motor controller must adapt to the time varying motor characteristics and maintain the performance in its long service life. The controller also should be robust against external disturbances like load disturbances, measurement noise etc. This paper presents the design of robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> speed controller for BLDC servo drive to address the problems mentioned above. The H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> speed controller is designed and simulations are carried out in MATLAB/SIMULINK and its performance is compared with a PI controller.

articleTitle: Five-level NPC/H-bridge MLI based electric spring for harmonic reduction and voltage regulation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Electric Spring is new emerging technology for stabilizing future smart grid. Due to integration of renewable energy sources with conventional one, new technological problem arises causing voltage instability in power grid. Electric spring is device which is effective in stabilizing voltage of system in decentralized manner and is more reliable over centralized way. Electric Spring is implemented earlier with using two level inverter, but this paper focused on implementation of Electric Spring using a special type of multilevel inverter i.e. NPC/H Bridge inverter. NPC/H Bridge inverter is further extension of Neutral point clamped inverter (NPC) and show additional effective features over NPC. Simulation is carried out using MATLAB/SIMULINK sucessfully showing comparision of Two-level, Three-level cascaded and Five-level NPC/H-bridge inverter THD's (Total Hormonic Distortion). ES based NPC/H bridge inverter successfully provides superior high frequency harmonic suppression along with improved system THD profile and effective voltage regulation.

articleTitle: Small signal stability analysis of DFIG based wind farms connected to SMIB
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: In this paper, SMIB is modified with connecting Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) via short transmission line is considered for small-signal stability analysis. The modified system without DFIG converter controller (MSMIB) has been analyzed using eigenvalues, participation factor and time domain simulation. Performance of MSMIB is evaluated at different operating points and DFIG wind speeds. The comparative analysis between MSMIB and SMIB has been done. The analysis clearly show the influence of DFIG on SMIB system.

articleTitle: Dual three phase induction motor control using Five Leg Inverter
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: This paper presents the Dual Induction Motor Control using Single Five Leg Inverter (FLI). The Inverter used in this technique consists of Five Leg's instead of Six Leg's as used in conventional drive control for two induction motors. The main objective of this FLI technique to incorporate this work to reduce the switching elements and which will eventually reduce the cost, weight and size of the drive technology. The Industries are looking performance improvements where the FLI technique can be integrated to multi motor control. In this proposed work the Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation Technique (SPWM) is used to control dual motors fed to FLI system. The output voltage and current waveform depends on the switching schemes applied to drive control system. The SPWM switching technique found to be most useful and suitable method when employed with dual motors connected to single inverter system. This paper investigates the independent speed control of two induction motors at different speeds connected to voltage source inverter system using MATLAB/SIMULINK Software.

articleTitle: A closed loop system to stabilize a 24V solar DC Nano grid
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Even though there is a vast advancement in the generation of electricity, some of the rural areas do not have access to it. An approach towards achieving rural electrification is the use of a solar DCNanogrid which can generate and distribute power to about a distance of 1 Km reliably. Since, most of the sources and loads are DC in nature, we can reduce the number of converter stages compared to an AC system. In this paper, we propose the idea of a closed loop system to stabilize the variations in the output of a DC Nano grid. This can be accomplished by using a solar panel as the source of energy and fixing the bus voltage level to be 24V along with a buck boost converter to obtain the required voltage level. This work is being demonstrated on a few home appliances such as motor, fan, TV, LED, mixer, grinder etc.

articleTitle: Mitigation of harmonics using hysteresis control technique of VSI based active power filter
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The rapid growth in the usage of non-linear loads such as Electric Arc Furnace (EAF), Induction motors etc. affects the power quality in the system. Some of the major power quality problems in the distribution system are voltage flickers, harmonics, power loss etc. In this paper a time domain model of EAF is proposed and designed, which uses an Active Power Filter (APF) for injection of current in the distribution system. PI controller and Hysteresis controller has been designed in this paper for control of APF. The performance of APF based EAF model is proposed and analyzed for three phase system and verified by the simulation in MATLAB/SIMULINK for.

articleTitle: An analysis of time current characteristics of adaptive inverse definite minimum time (IDMT) overcurrent relay for symmetrical and un-symmetrical faults
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The paper presents the analysis of the time current characteristics (TCC) of the IDMT overcurrent relays. Overcurrent relays are subjected to the change in conditions of time delay (TD), Pickup settings and PSM (Plug Setting Multiplier) which are an essential substance for adaptive relaying. Overcurrent relays should operate reliably during the normal operations and enhanced fault conditions. Alteration in different parameters results in adaptive setting of overcurrent relays, according to the fault conditions and its values. During analysis, the IDMT overcurrent relay settings which are TD and PSM is infused according the protection level required for the different level of faults and load current. Variation of fault is perceived and TCC curve is analysed, which is then altered to acquire the optimum level of protection. The research is primarily focused on the behaviour of overcurrent relay parameters by changing the assessment effectively through analysis of the TCC curve by analysing the fault current in power system. Substantial flexibility aids in superior adjustment of overcurrent relay to ensure adequate device coordination. Effective and reliable analysis of the curve helps in the compelling reassurance of the power system protection.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of dual port SRAM memory architecture using MOSFET's
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Dual port memory cell is the multiport memory cell that provides required access to multi-processor applications. It uses two additional pass transistors, bit line pair and a word line to provide much needed simultaneous access. Each SRAM cell is accessed by dual ports with devoted word and bit lines to each. Single port SRAM allows access to only single address of a memory cell at a time during each clock pulse but dual port overcomes this drawback and allows concurrent read or write access at different addresses. Thus the efficiency is almost doubled by using dual port RAM. The most important benefit of dual port RAM is that they will not have limitations of access between the two ports, as each processor can be made to operate at different clock frequencies.

articleTitle: Target tracking using adaptive Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: In this paper Ballistic missile is tracked in re-entry phase using Extended Kalman Filter(EKF) which is mainly used in nonlinear estimation. Target tracking of Ballistic Missile has been done using EKF and further the result of EKF is compared with Adaptive extended Kalman filter (AEKF). The basic difference between them is that EKF use a priori guess to estimate the process and measurement noise while AEKF updates them in every measurement step but with the regular change in the circumstances priori guess can be estimated with larger error hence AEKF can stand better in that case. The simulation results show that AEKF is better in performance as compared to EKF in terms of accuracy as well as covariance.

articleTitle: Power quality improvement and mitigation of harmonic distortion using DSTATCOM with PI and Fuzzy Logic Controller
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: In the last decade there has been an upsurge in the development of improved power conditioning devices due to the latest upheaval in the applications of custom power devices (CPDs). CPDs offer several advantages over conventional capacitor and inductor banks which tends to be bulkier, lossy, poor reliability and overall poor control and lower efficiency. Therefore, this paper presents a new array of utilization of CPDs involving DSTATCOM which is by far the most versatile device among several others for power quality improvement at the distribution side. Reliability and quality are the two most important facets of any power delivery system. The prime focus will be to comprehend various occurrences of faults in an interconnected transmission network and devising possible ways to mitigate those faults using DSTATCOM. Power Electronic converters have played a pivotal role in the control of power quality mainly due to their fast action, reliability and lower cost in comparison to conventional electro-mechanical controllers. To obtain the desired objective IGBT based Voltage Source Converter (VSC) operating at high frequencies using Sinusoidal Pulse Width Modulation (SPWM) is used. For efficient reduction in harmonic contents passive LCL filter is used at the Point of Common Connection (PCC). Analysis involving both PI and Fuzzy Logic Controller is shown in the simulation results. Comparative analysis and pros and cons involving both the proposed control topologies are discussed. Here various kinds of faults commonly occurring in a power system are induced and their impact on power quality is monitored. All the simulation is done using MATLAB Simulink using SimPower System Blockset (PSB) Toolbox.

articleTitle: 16-Bit GDI multiplier design for low power applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Today, more and more, high speed mobile computational devices and equipments are being introduced in the market. These computational devices strain and drain the battery very quickly. Researchers are making efforts to find ways and means to conserve the battery power for longer period. The core key components in these computational devices are the Multipliers to support high speed computational intensive applications in real time. Thus it becomes more important to reduce power dissipation and area in these multiplier modules as they affect the performance of the device. Several VLSI design techniques have been attempted to optimize the power and area occupied by the multiplier module, but there are very few design techniques that gives the required extensibility both in terms of power and area. In this paper a high speed, reliable and efficient 16 bit multiplier VLSImodule design is presented using GDI (Gate Diffusion Input) technique, addressing both power consumption and area complexity. Further, comparative study results of the proposed design over the traditional CMOS design are also presented. Detailed design steps and comparative study using Cadence Virtuoso simulation tool at 180nm CMOS technology is discussed. The simulation results presented show reduction in both power and area of the proposed design at 1.8Vsupply voltage.

articleTitle: Experimental analysis of symmetrical & asymmetrical PWM based single phase AC chopper for power quality improvement using FPGA real time controller
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: A 1-phase AC chopper circuit is rigged up and analyzed with single phase induction motor for input power factor, harmonic profile and efficiency of the converter using FPGA real time controller. The various PWM techniques such as symmetrical ramp-DC PWM (SRDPWM), asymmetrical ramp-triangular PWM (ARTPWM), asymmetrical sinusoidal PWM type-1 [ASPWM1] and asymmetrical sinusoidal PWM type-2 [ASPWM2] techniques are generated using FPGA real time controller in order to analyze these electrical parameters. It is observed from experimental results that the SRDPWM technique gives lesser total harmonic distortion [THD] of output voltage and input current than other techniques. It is also observed that the ASPWM1 switching strategy gives high input power factor, more output voltage and high efficiency and moderate improvement of harmonic profile for the entire range of modulation index MI compared to other PWM techniques. Hence ASPWM1 technique is preferred for AC chopper for better input power factor, output voltage, harmonic profile and efficiency of the converter than other techniques that renders easy filteration at lower cost.

articleTitle: Enhancement of oscillatory response of DFIG based wind energy conversion system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: This paper deals with analysis of Torsional Interaction (TI) phenomenon in a wind energy conversion system based on doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) with series compensation network. Mathematical modelling of induction machine, two mass shaft, transmission line, rotor-side-converter (RSC) and grid-side-converter (GSC) controllers is developed using dynamic equations. The simulation is carried out on a 3.73kW wind farm and the effect on turbine-generator shaft oscillations due to addition of capacitance on distribution side is studied. This capacitance may cause resonance with inductance effect, therefore oscillations are likely to occur. In addition, the rotor-side-converter and the grid-side-converter controllers are explored to damp out the oscillations.

articleTitle: Genetic algorithm and reconfiguration for loss minimization in radial distribution system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: This paper emphasizes on the optimal reconfiguration of distribution system in order to decrease the active power losses and in turn enhance the quality of power in the distribution system. The method also helps in improving voltage profile of the system as a whole. The optimization of the system is constrained by the radial configuration format, bus isolation issues and abnormal cases of combinations. The methodology is applied on to the 33 bus test system assuming constant loads and the study findings comprise of the optimal configuration of switches given by genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of a novel bifurcated winding induction generator by finite element model
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Induction machines are popular in the industry due to its reliability, ruggedness, simplicity and cost. Cage rotor induction generators are being replaced by doubly-fed induction generator configurations. However, in this paper an attempt is made to highlight the specific features of a cage rotor bifurcated winding induction generator configuration found suitable for variable speed applications especially in the area of wind energy systems. The study based on finite element models (FEM) offers more information on the phenomena characterizing the operation of electrical machines than the classical analytical models and is convenient to develop especially if the machine is asymmetrical in its winding configuration. A model of the machine is developed using Ansys and its performance under various conditions successfully compared with the experimental results obtained on the actual machine.

articleTitle: A PID controller tuning rule for FOPDT process to achieve better load disturbance rejection based on maximum sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: In this paper, the PID tuning rule for first order plus dead time (FOPDT) process has been proposed to achieve better load disturbance rejection. The tuning rule is derived in terms of maximum sensitivity (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) only which is based on the pole placement and frequency response matching criteria. The maximum sensitivity (M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) is the only tuning parameter of the controller which is the desired robustness level and thus by fixing the M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> value the PID parameters can be directly evaluated. The proposed method is applicable to integrating plus dead time (IPDT) process by considering the poles very near to zero and approximating it to FOPDT process. The method is also applicable to higher order process by approximating the process to FOPDT process. The proposed method is illustrated through different examples and compared with some of the well known method available in the literature.

articleTitle: A simplified space vector pulse width modulation for three phase three-level diode clamped inverter
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: For diode clamped multilevel inverter topology dc link capacitor balancing is a vital issue. Proper switching sequence in space vector pulse width modulation plays a pivotal role in this regard without introducing any extra controller. This paper proposes SVPWM algorithm with seven segment switching sequence for three level inverter against the switching sequences where all the switching states along with their redundant states were used and detail comparison between those two sequence of SVPWM are discussed. Finaly, the operation of proposed algorithm is verified through MATLAB/SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: Modified differential evolution algorithm for optimal power flow with FACTS devices
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: This paper investigates potential of modified differential evolution (MDE) algorithm, to find solution for optimal power flow (OPF) problem of power system. The performance of the proposed MDE algorithm is experienced on the modified IEEE-30 bus test systems integrating flexible ac transmission systems (FACTS) devices, that is, thyristor controlled phase shifter (TCPS) and thyristor controlled series capacitor (TCSC) at preset locations. The OPF problem of the present work is formulated with five different objective functions viz. (a) fuel cost (with valve point effect) minimization, (b) power transmission losses minimization, (c) emission reduction (d) fuel cost (without valve point effect) minimization and (e) minimization of combined economic and environmental cost. The proposed implementation exploits MDE, resulting in a much shorter execution time while retaining the best possible solution of OPF problem.

articleTitle: Bacteria foraging optimized and modified PSO optimized PD-SMC and PID-SMC controller for inverted pendulum system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: In this paper, sliding mode controller (SMC) is designed for trajectory tracking of Inverted Pendulum (IP) system. In order to determine the optimized parameters for the controller two optimization techniques are used. In this work, Bacteria Foraging (BFOA) method and Modified Particle Swarm Optimized (MPSO) methods are used. The controller is basically designed for trajectory tracking and stabilization of nonlinear single stage inverted pendulum. A sliding mode controller (SMC) is well known for nonlinear system controlling and it is a robust method which has higher convergence. This paper throws light on sliding surface design. Proportional and Derivative (PD) and Proportional Integral and Derivative (PID) sliding surface based sliding mode controllers are designed. Using Lyapunov stability approach control law of sliding mode is derived and its asymptotic stability proved mathematically.

articleTitle: Multiple output push-pull converter with post regulated buck converters
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Switched Mode Power Supplies (SMPS) play a vital role in the field of Power electronic systems. They can be found to be in use in a variety of power processing applications, ranging from lower power applications such as on-chip power management to high power applications such as power systems. In this paper, a multiple output push-pull DC-DC converter is designed and simulated. The power module can supply multiple voltage levels from an input battery. Among the multiple outputs, the Master output or the output with the maximum voltage will be fed back directly using closed loop compensation circuitry. The feedback line will be isolated to maintain a complete galvanic isolation between primary and secondary sides of the circuit. The slave outputs or the lesser voltage outputs will be post regulated using buck converters. The design of the circuit elements for the post regulated buck converters will be done with help of the tool LTpowerCAD. The simulations were done in LTSpice environment. The simulation results show that a stable output is obtained across all the three output ports.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of half-bridge LLC resonant converter with integrated transformer for compact design
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Higher power densities in SMPC circuits can be achieved by operating converter at high switching frequencies, which can reduce size of passive components. Operating at higher switching frequencies with hard switching leads to increase in switching losses. By using soft-switching methods, switching losses can be reduced. It is preferred to use Half-Bridge LLC resonant converter operating under Zero-Voltage switching (ZVS) for entire load range, ZVS is obtained by oscillations made by the LLC resonant tank. By designing resonant tank inductances using Integrated transformer makes converter more compact. Half-Bridge LLC resonant converter switches are driven by pulse frequency modulation (PFM) technique using external IC. This LLC resonant converter is designed to operate between 90kHzs to 55kHzs from no load to full load respectively. In this paper, equivalent circuit analysis of resonant tank with integrated transformer, design procedure, experimental results and waveforms are presented to validate design for 80W model.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of pulsed output interleaved flyback converter with lossless snubber and current mode control
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The Electronic Power Controller (EPC) requires high power pulses for the transmission of data with high precision in communication fields. In order to achieve this requirement, Interleaved flyback design is considered which has the added advantage of reduction in source power requirement by half and due to high frequency operation of the switches of the converter. The voltage across the converter is controlled using Lossless snubber topology and thereby increasing the overall efficiency of the EPC greater than 80% and voltage stress across the MOSFET is less than 180V. In this work, design and implementation of the Lossless snubber and Current slope compensation are adopted in EPC to generate high precision 2.5kHz, 28V to drive 2.5A load with 80% efficiency.

articleTitle: Estimation of Arc voltage characteristic for high current fault Arcs
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Generally, arc models are used to study the behaviour of the electric arc and its interaction with the circuit. Precise simulation of fault current arc has very important role in performing arc flash calculations for short circuit test and arc test on different electrical equipment and also for fault analysis in power system studies. It is also very useful in deciding the test parameters during short circuit testing. This paper discusses the several arc models for calculating the arc voltage for various arc fault currents. These models are compared with the real-time testing carried out at High Power lab, CPRI, Bangalore.

articleTitle: Multiple output fly back converter with primary side current mode control for defence applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Switched Mode Power Supplies (SMPS) have a crucial role to play in present defense and space applications. SMPS are enabled to give a desired output voltage by controlling the PWM pulses given to the gate of the switching device. This paper is focused on design and implementation of current mode controlled multiple output flyback converter. Flyback topology makes the converter module more compact. The proposed converter delivers output voltages of 15V/1A, -15/1A and 5V/3A. The converter is switching at a frequency of 200 KHz and primary side current mode control technique is implemented using UCC28C43 Pulse Width Modulation Integrated Circuit (PWM IC). This will reduce transformer size and increases efficiency. Post regulators are used to achieve better line and load regulation. The converter is also provided with features such as under voltage, Short circuit and over temperature protection. Hardware implementation of converter module is done and results are validated.

articleTitle: A hybrid modular multilevel converter topology with modified phase-shifted carrier pulse-width modulation scheme
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) topology is getting popularized for the medium to high voltage applications after its inception. This paper presents a modified topology of the conventional MMC, named as Hybrid MMC (HMMC). This topology has reduced number of switch counts than the conventional MMC. Therefore, it is more efficient and has less complex circuitry than other existing multi-level topologies. In this paper a modified phase-shifted carrier pulse width modulation scheme (PS-PWM) is used for the switching of HMMC. The three-phase circuit is simulated in the Matlab/Simulink for different load conditions and the results are provided to validate the concepts behind the topology.

articleTitle: Fault-ride through capability of a distribution system with diesel, solar and wind distributed generators
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The main aim of this work is to study the impact of penetrating Diesel, Solar and wind distributed generators into a 27 bus, 69kV/100 MVA distribution system. The 27 buses, 69kV, 100MVA distribution system along with distributed generators was designed & modeled in DIgSILENT Power Factory. A dynamic P-Q control for VSC of solar generator was designed. A dynamic electrical control (P-Q for Rotor VSC, Vdc-Q for Grid VSC) was designed for the control of back-to-back converters of Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG). The stability of all distributed generators in grid connected mode for a 3ph short circuit fault was studied. The impact of distributed generators on unforeseen increase in fault currents was observed and nature of distributed generators was analyzed by monitoring the fault current for a 3ph short circuit fault. The fault ride through capability of distribution system in the presence of distributed generators was investigated by correlating critical clearing time (CCT) for a 3ph short circuit fault and electrical distance (ED) between fault bus and distributed generator bus.

articleTitle: Minimization of torque ripple using DITC with optimum bandwidth and switching frequency for SRM employed in electric vehicle
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: This paper presents the modeling and simulation of two-level and three-level Direct Instantaneous Torque Controller (DITC) for Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) employed in electric vehicle. DITC is implemented taking torque as control variable and is estimated from the look-up table by considering current and rotor position of SRM. Further, PI controller is designed using symmetrical optimum method and integrated with two-level torque controller. Performance of two-level torque controller with and without PI controller is observed in terms of torque ripple for various bandwidths and switching frequency. It is observed that, the contribution of PI controller in terms of torque ripple minimization is not remarkable. In this regard, three-level torque controller is implemented in order to achieve the better performance and desired features for the operation of SRM in electric vehicle (EV). Finally, performances of two-level and three-level torque controller are compared in terms of minimum torque ripple, wide speed operation, high starting torque and converter switching frequency. It is observed that three-level torque controller has better performance than two-level controller for SRM employed in electric vehicle.

articleTitle: Pencil drawn films as Ammonia gas sensors
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Pencil drawn films, are found to be chemiresistors. Pencil lead, an everyday commodity, is a composite of graphite and clay and pencil drawn films have been used to sense acetone, ethyl acetate, hexane, methanol, THF, toluene and N0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Use of Pencil drawn films on KAPTON substrate as ammonia sensor has been demonstrated in this work; the resistance of these films increase on exposure to ammonia. Importance of expressing sensitivity taking into account gas concentration has been discussed. Sensitivity varies from 46E-3%/ppm to 1.96E-3%/ppm over the concentration range of 39ppm to 2684ppm. Design of a portable ammonia alarm with wearable sensor using Arduino board has been presented. This can be a very useful product for use in chemical plants, agricultural lands, labs etc.

articleTitle: Performanceanalysis of open end winding induction motor drive using center spaced PWM and bus clamping PWM techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: In this paper, space vector based decoupled bus clamping PWM techniques are proposed for open-end winding induction motor drive fed with conventional two level inverters on either side. The switching vectors for the conventional inverters are generated using instantaneous reference voltages along with the simple digital logic. All the proposed bus-clamped PWM techniques are generated by phase shifting the one inverter reference phase voltages by 180 degrees with respect to the other inverter. A common-mode voltage is identified in the open-end winding induction motor drive. All the space vector based decoupled bus-clamping PWM techniques proposed in this work are to reduce the common mode voltage by greater extent and also give less switching loss compared to center spaced space vector PWM technique. To validate the proposed work, several simulation studies has been carried out in MATLAB/SIMULINK and the corresponding results are presented and compared.

articleTitle: Preprocessing of experimental partial discharge signalsin insulation samples using adaptive signal processing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The pre-processing of the Partial Discharge (PD) signal is very important and crucial stage in analyzing condition of the electrical insulation. The PD information is lost in the presence of various noises. The wavelet based adaptive Thresholding de-noising techniques are well suited for reducing the noise. This paper considers the various adaptive thresholding techniques such as Heursure, Minimaxi, VisuShrink, SureShrink, thresholding methods for denoising of the PD signals obtained in various insulation samples using the experimental setup. The PD pulses produced by the insulation samples were detected in the form of discharges through the impedance and is fed through a cable to the PD detector along with a amplitude modulating signal. The developed Wavelet Transform based adaptive thresholding algorithm suitably removes the interferences from the measured PD signals. The performance indices are evaluated which justifies the strength of the algorithm in denoising of experimental PD data.

articleTitle: Design & fabrication of small scale horizontal axis wind turbine and performance analysis of the turbine
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The use of renewable energy is growing rapidly in the modern trend. Specially, wind turbines have been playing a great role in the generation of electricity and moreover their use has been increasing for electrification. Small scale wind turbine power have become very useful where low power is required; however, complex design makes it expensive and unreliable to use for low power. The research is primarily focused on the preliminary design & its fabrication and the considerations for designing of the 500W horizontal axis wind turbine (HAWT) system. Moreover, it is concentrated on power extraction and the performance of the system and emphasized on the utilization of wind for optimum power extraction. The generator uses permanent neodymium magnet of very high strength in the alternator for the generation of the power. Performance analysis of the wind turbine helps in analysis of output power, voltage, current, rpm and wind speed. The model system of the small scale wind turbine is significantly important particularly in the rural electrification and promotion of renewable energies as a form of green and clean energy.

articleTitle: Flyback topology based multi-output pulsed power supply with planar magnetic technology and current mode control method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Transceivers in satellites need Pulsed Power to generate RF signals. The Quality of the RF signals is mainly depends on High frequency voltage with minimum rise time, fall time and output ripple. Pulsed power leads to discharge of High current in very short interval of time. This creates a challenge of designing High current handling capable Power supply with tight load regulation and quick transient response. This Paper presents DC-DC 10 Output Fly-back converter which generates eight, 3.7kHz Pulsed voltages of 65% and 10% duty cycle, 1 Positive and 1 Negative continuous voltage with more than 60% Efficiency. The Planar transformer is used to reduce the Leakage inductance and Complexity of assembly. Current mode control method with proper phase compensation is used for Quick Transient Response. Closed loop Output regulators improve the load regulation and control the rise time and fall time of Pulsed Outputs. Planar Transformer along with RCD clamp circuit reduces the Drain and Source Voltage stress in MOSFET and increases the lifetime of it. The Over current protection circuit and EMI filter circuit increase reliability of the converter. The Radiation Hardened semiconductor devices, Hybrid Micro circuits and Shielded Mechanical structure of the converter make it to fit for Hazardous Space environment. The Design and Experimental results of Converter are shown in this paper.

articleTitle: A MSP430 controller based class-D audio power amplifier with DLDPC PWM switching
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: An audio power amplifier system is used worldwide for the amplification of audio signals without any distortion and with high efficiency. The audio signals are obtained from different source of inputs and the amplifier system adopts different topologies of amplifiers in realizing the system. In this paper, an audio power amplifier system uses Class-D topology which adopts Dual Line Dual Phase Carrier (DLDPC) Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) technique to effectively reduce the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) as well as to increase the Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR). Also the system takes care of the switching losses caused by low amplitude inputs through adopting the power supply switching strategy thus reducing the effect of low modulation index. The MSP430 micro controller is a low power controller used as control unit for the system which monitors and handle faults while providing additional functionalities to the system.

articleTitle: Analytical modelling, simulation, and comparative study of compound alloy based tandem solar cells — An efficient way of renewable energy management
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The most efficient technology for generation of electricity from solar irradiation is multijunction solar cell in tandem structure. The materials used in these structures are a prime factor, controlling device efficiency. The III-V compound semiconductor optoelectronic alloys are quite promising, due to their direct bandgap feature and superior performance, compared to any other existing solar cell technologies. This has led to a widespread use of these alloys in solar panels installed in satellites. In spite of superior performance of III-V alloy cells, Si cells have dominated the terrestrial market due to their lower cost. To introduce cost effectiveness in tandem cells Al is alloyed with GaInP and GaAs, in the proposed structures, which bring down the cost of these priceless alloys. Moreover, a comparative analysis is done among double and triple junction cells. The aim of this work is to investigate and correlate their performance in terms of efficiency, fill factor, and other electrical parameters, in double junction and triple junction solar cell on Germanium (Ge) substrate. Dark current of these two cells are also calculated for analyzing their performance.

articleTitle: A novel approach for partial discharge pattern recognition based on FP3CM-ENN
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Partial Discharge (PD) pattern recognition is a main tool for assessing the insulating ability of high voltage (HV) equipment. A new PD identification method found on the fuzzy-possibilistic product partition c-means (FP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>CM) — extension neural network (ENN) for HV equipment is proposed in this paper. A PD detector is familiar to assess the PD patterns. The Statistical feature extraction method is adapted to take out the features for every PD pattern. This advanced method combines the FP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>CM clustering algorithm with the ENN architecture. The FP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>CM is framed by the product of probabilistic and possibilistic fuzzy partitions instead of linear combination. This clustering model produces very accurate partitions in the existence of noise data. The centers of the FP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>CM are used as the initial centers of the ENN. The FP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>CM-ENN algorithm adopts extension distance to compute the resemblance among tested data and cluster centers. This proposed FP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>CM-ENN algorithm procures the benefit of high precision, robustness and less memory consumption, that are helpful in PD recognition. To verify the efficacy of the suggested method, similar studies with a MLP, ENN, fuzzy c means (FCM) — ENN, Possibilistic FCM (PFCM) — ENN are carried out for different samples with rather encouraging results.

Author Keywords: fuzzy possibilistic product partition c means

articleTitle: Newton-Raphson's successive approximation method based TCSC controller
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Transient voltage stability is a crucial and very rapid phenomenon that requires a very quick and accurate response to prevent voltage collapse in an AC system. One of the methods to prevent this situation is by using Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS) controllers. This paper proposes a method that is based on the control of Thyristor Controlled Series Compensator (TCSC) from the Micro-controller so that the voltage stability requirement can be met easily. The proposed method is aimed to provide a quick response to prevent voltage collapse using a micro-controller, wherein, the Newtons-Raphson's approximation method is used for calculation of the conduction angle and thus the gating pulses are provided to the TCSC controller.

articleTitle: Sensors and control system models for wind power generation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Wind power is one of the rapidly developing sectors in every part of the world, with growth rates ranging from 10 to 40% per year. The major challenges faced are improvements in the performance of the system and reduction in the investment cost and operating cost. To reduce the payback period and provide the impetus for investment and widespread acceptance of this clean energy source, reduction of operating cost is an essential requirement. To improve the performance of the system and increase the reliability, it is important that the turbine reacts to the external environment appropriately. A key solution to this would be to have sensors installed at right place and design a good control system. This paper includes application of sensors and designing of important control systems of wind turbine like pitch control, yaw control, temperature control. The vibration analysis also has been presented. Apart from this, the fault analysis is carried out to ensure the safety of wind turbine.

articleTitle: Power supply for smart meters
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Power supplies are primarily used to provide needed output voltage by suitably controlling the pulse width modulated (PWM) signal given to the gate of the quick acting power electronics switches. Smart meter are put up in use in smart grid that is exposed to continuous fluctuations at the load and as well as the grid supply side, thus smart meter employed should have the power supplies having faster response to these fluctuations. This paper presents implementation of a power supply with top Switch as switch device. The designed device is determined to have a good output voltage regulation and better efficiency for the wide input voltage range.

articleTitle: Integration of wind farm to VSC-HVDC system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Renewable energy resources are playing an important role in reducing the energy crisis. One of the important resources is being wind energy systems. Most of the times, offshore wind power is transferred to the main land grid through VSC-HVDC transmission system due to its advantages. As converters are required for transmission of offshore power, their control mechanism takes a major control overpower transmission. In this work a power system is proposed, wherein a high penetration no storage wind diesel isolated system (HPNSWD) is interconnected to an existing VSC-HVDC system, in order to enhance the power transfer capability of a 200KV, 500MW VSC-HVDC system.

articleTitle: Design of 60 Ghz CMOS power amplifier to improve power added efficiency
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: This discourse used 45nm CMOS technology to model a power amplifier of class AB for a Power Added Efficiency (PAE) of 23% and power gain of lOdB at the 60GHz unlicensed band of frequency. This CMOS class-AB Power Amplifier (PA) is one of the important stages to enhance the power output of the transmitter chain. Here the designed power amplifier can be used for short range communication of 4m-20m applicable for Bluetooth operations. The proposed class AB amplifier yields a maximum efficiency of 68% at 60GHz. Common source configuration is employed in the driver stage to enhance the output power with single stage contours. Load stage is basically a MOS connected back to back to get the maximum output. A class AB power amplifier is adopted for its high power efficiency and better linearity. The measurement results indicated that the input match and the output gain at 60GHz achieves −18dB and 12dB respectively with the supply voltage of 900mV. The frequency response obtained is a narrow band response with 6GHz of bandwidth. Using Cadence Virtuoso tool circuit is simulated. Using Virtuoso Layout Editor the layout of the associated circuit is drawn with the total size of 0.107um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Improving system performance using electric spring with current source inverters
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Electric springs is the technology to overcome problems caused due to the penetration of renewable energy. The electric spring maintains constant voltage to the critical loads and passes the fluctuation to the non-critical loads. Electric springs were realizedusing voltage source inverters. Here electric springs is realizedusing current source inverter and using a new control called direct current control. This helps in reducing THD values across critical load. Along with direct current control a harmonic suppression feature is also added along with direct current control. This control enables to get a clean and sinusoidal waveform across critical load. The direct current control is achieved using hysteresis current control. For harmonic suppression function the input current is separated into real and imaginary components with the help of the single-phase dqO transformation. By using this control strategy, the THD values of CL voltages can be greatly reduced thereby improving system performance. The proposed strategy is simulated in MATLAB Simulink platform.

articleTitle: HIT solar cell using ZnTe as an emitter layer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: This work is concentrated on a new structure of HIT solar cell using Zinc Telluride (ZnTe) material along with a-Si and c-Si. The proposed structure ITO/ZnTe(p)/a-Si(i)/c-Si(n)/a-Si(n)/ITO is modeled and observed a Significant solar cell efficiency of 27.7%. The thicknesses of the layers are varied to show the relation between the thickness and the performance of the solar cell. The HIT solar structure is developed in AFORS-HET Simulating tool.

articleTitle: Induction motor drive based modelling and simulation approach for anchor operation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: One of the essential operations performed when the shipping vessel is parked in the middle of the sea or at the deck is Anchoring. This is very critical because the vessel has to be in the stationary position on water and does not drift unnecessarily from its position due to water currents and wind. The conventional anchoring is largely manual involving huge manpower using hydraulic operations for the movement of anchor and chain mounted on the drum of the vessel. Use of a Variable frequency drive with an induction motor methodology is proposed in this paper. This performs the anchor operation with high accuracy and is safe with minimized human effort.

articleTitle: Automatic testing of medium voltage drive using OPC server interface
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: This paper investigates automatic testing of medium voltage drive controller using OPC server interface. OPC is a standard software interface that allows Windows program to communicate with industrial hardware devices. The control board of medium voltage drive consists of digital input signals, which are used to control the drive e.g. drive start, stop and analog signals for giving speed or torque reference to the motor. In field these signals are given through another controller e.g. PLC that serve as a master. These signals can also be generated manually using control panel. In automatic testing of the drive application software, these control signals are to be accessed by Automatic Testing Framework. Using OPC server interface in Visual Studio solution it is possible to access the PLC symbol variables and control the drive for application software functionality testing. PLC symbol variables are accessed by Automatic Testing Framework through OPC gateway server. This paper describes the hardware setup, environment used for MV drive under test and automatic testing of control software using OPC Server Interface. Test results provided here proves the advantage of using OPC interface over conventional way of testing.

articleTitle: A fixed frequency ZVS integrated boost dual three-phase bridge DC-DC LCL-type series resonant converter for large power applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The design of a converter as an example of a high power (>10 kW), fixed frequency controlled three-phase DC-DC LCL-type series resonant converter (SRC) with integrated boost function is described. The specifications of the converter are chosen to match the rating of a linear generator (LG) used in wave energy generation application. The performance of the designed converter has been verified by using PSIM simulation software. The zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) of all the switches is accomplished by designing the converter to operate in the lagging pf mode for a wide input voltage and load variations. Theoretical and simulation results have been compared and presented in the form of a table. Power loss break-down analysis of the designed converter has been done and the summary of results is presented.

articleTitle: Modified fuzzy logic technique for power transformer fault prediction
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Power transformer forms a very important link in the power system. A fault in transformer can cause a huge loss to the utility and consumer depending on the duration of the outage. Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) acts as a key tool to diagnose faults in transformer based on gas ratios. In this paper an effort to predict Power transformer fault more precisely using modified fuzzy logic technique has been attempted. DGA data of various transformer oil samples were collected and analyzed to prove that the modified fuzzy logic technique provides a better accurate prediction.

articleTitle: Estimation of severity of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis using signal processing techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Loss of motor neurons leads to Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in human beings. It is characterized by altered gait rhythm. In this work, gait data is collected from both normal and pathological subjects. Data collected in each case is divided into multiple blocks and average value of each block is found. Number of times signals crossing average value is found. Depending on the result obtained in each case and in comparison with normal, severity estimation is made.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of power electronic converters in wind turbine system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: Wind power generation is experiencing a tremendous growth over the past few decades in terms of the individual turbine size as well as the total installed capacity. Power electronics has played a significant role in bringing about this change as they are a technical solution to wind turbine's electrical difficulties. This paper analyses the need for power electronic converters in wind turbine systems. Nowadays, the proportion of power integrated into the grid is accelerating at a very fast pace. A grid fault might lead to a decline in the voltage (dip) resulting in an extensive tripping of the wind turbines leading to voltage instabilities and blackouts. To ensure continuous operation, low voltage ride through (LVRT) requirements of the wind turbines must be met. LVRT is achieved by using energy storage devices. High voltage ride through prevents the occurrence of overvoltage conditions across the network by using a crowbar circuit arrangement across the DC link. In this paper, a 2MW wind turbine system (WTS) employing a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) connected to the network through a back-to-back power converter is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. From the results, it can be observed that to meet the interconnection requirements of the grid such as voltage, frequency, power, harmonics, etc. with the wind turbine characteristics, it is essential to employ power converters. Control system on generator side converter is designed to control the speed of the PMSG to ensure Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) while the grid side converter control system controls the DC link bus voltage and the sinusoidal nature of the voltage and current given to the grid.

Author Keywords: Generator and grid side converter control

articleTitle: Robust control analysis using μ-synthesis for nonlinear control system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to analyze the non-linear system for its robustness which is controlled by Type 1 Fuzzy GA controller. The control object is to control temperature of the system. System is Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR), which exhibits highly non-linear dynamics. The process taking place in this CSTR is cooling only. Process Reaction curve is used to have system temperature response. In this paper, system is tuned with the help of intelligent optimization technique, and then analyzed the response in MATLAB Simulink model. Both PID and Fuzzy GA controllers are designed and implemented on CSTR for temperature control. Both results are compared and robust analysis of system is done with the help of μ synthesis. Robust analysis of the system is carried out to ensure the stability of the system. For given weight value we checked the robust stability of the system.

articleTitle: Simulation study of partial shading effect on series, parallel and series-parallel connected PV modules
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: A mathematical model of photovoltaic (PV) cell based on single diode model has developed using Matlab/Simulink. The model has option to simulate the Output Power versus Output Voltage (P-V) and Output Current versus Output Voltage (I-V) characteristics of PV cell under the effect of uniform/partial changes in irradiations and also under the effect of change in operating temperature, series resistance, shunt resistance, ideality factor of the PV cell. The simulation results of PV cell, PV module and different arrangements of PV modules under various operating conditions has included and investigation on the effect of partial shading on PV array also is discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: A novel Power Factor Correction technique For single phase AC to DC conversion
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: In this paper, an advanced control technique based on Pulse Width Modulation is proposed for Power Factor Correction in Single Phase AC/DC Interleaved Boost Converter in boundary conduction mode at a variable switching frequency. The basic idea behind interleaving is to parallelize the converter channels with a common input/ output filter and load. The driving signal for N phase interleaved converters has 2WN phase-shift to one another, thus providing shift in individual inductor currents and thereby reducing current ripples. The advantages are low input current ripple, better Total Harmonic Distortion factor, improved Power Factor Operation, faster transient response, reduced electromagnetic emission, high efficiency, low device stress and improved reliability. Mathematical analyses have been carried out along with closed loop simulation and designing of prototype replica.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a microgrid-fault response system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Smart grids, Power and Advanced Control Engineering (ICSPACE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach of fault detection and location within electrical power grids. As being vulnerable to various types of faults in the system: Line to Line(L-L), Line to Ground(L-G), Line to Line to Ground(L-L-G), Line to Line to Line to Ground(L-L-L-G), the grids also suffer due to the harmonics within the transmission line due to the increasing dependency and interconnection of Renewable energy sources to the grids. In this paper, the Indian transmission grid synchronized with Intelligent Electronic Devices(IEDs) are employed to get the system parameter values and transfer it real-time using Profibus to the microprocessor which then sends the data to the database. From the database, the data is then drawn into the SCADA control system and the operation of isolation of a faulty node is performed on the grid side. An Intelligent system is developed using Dynamic algorithm where the database filters the incoming data and directs the data according to the program into two different databases. Each database is used for the purpose of detecting the system status and identification of the type of fault along with its values. Fault prediction is performed where the approaching fault is detected so that appropriate measures may be implemented to prevent the occurrence of that specific fault. Thus, an efficient protection of smart grids from any expected fault and isolation ofthat specific node to prevent the spread of fault to other healthy nodes can be performed.
